name: Caphtor
overview: Caphtor is a male figure identified in Scripture as the son of Mizraim. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional tribal affiliation or detailed notes provided. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Caphtor appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:14. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is indicated in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Caphtor as a son of Mizraim, establishing a direct paternal relationship. No other family connections are noted beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Caphtor's significance lies in his placement within the genealogical records of Genesis, linking him to Mizraim, who is associated with Egypt. This connection situates Caphtor within the broader narrative of the nations descended from Noah's sons, highlighting God's sovereign hand in the formation of peoples. Though brief, his mention contributes to the biblical understanding of ethnic origins and God's providential ordering of history.
